name: Balkan brass (fanfara, Roma-Serbian-Macedonian)
lineage: Balkan brass ensemble tradition of southern Serbia (Vranje, Užice regions), western Bulgaria, and northern Macedonia, performed by predominantly Roma musicians at weddings, funerals, and the canonical annual Guča Brass Band Festival in southern Serbia (founded 1961). Performance configuration: ensemble of 6-12 brass instruments (trumpets, trombones, tubas, flugelhorns) plus tapan large frame-drum, playing characteristic Balkan asymmetrical-meter (5/8, 7/8, 9/8, 11/8) rhythmic-cycles with virtuosic ornamental melodic-line. The genre crystallized in nineteenth-century Ottoman-period military-band tradition adapted into the post-Ottoman Balkan civilian-popular-celebration context. Distinguished from neighboring Albanian saze and Greek nisiotika by Balkan brass's brass-ensemble (vs string-and-clarinet) instrumental signature.
